title: Sections of an fs log structure are integral and saturated
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme, with log structure on the small etale site and fs charts as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For an etale scheme $U\to X$, write $H=M(U)$ additively, and let $j:H\to H^{\rm gp}$ be its canonical map to its group completion. Then $j$ is injective, and for every $g\in H^{\rm gp}$ and every integer $n>0$, $ng\in j(H)$ implies $g\in j(H)$. Thus $M(U)$ is integral and saturated; finite generation of $M(U)$ is not asserted. This includes $U=X$ and the empty scheme, and imposes no torsion-freeness condition on $H^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69, fs charts; VIII 3.1.17, p.101, root saturation. Agent extraction of the stalk and sheaf consequences, not a separately stated theorem here. WANTED: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie (1988), section 1, integral and saturated log structures.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$. Choose an fs chart $P\to M$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood, as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $G=A^\times$ and $E=\beta^{-1}(A^\times)\subseteq P$, where $\beta:P\to A$ is the chart's structural map. The chart definition identifies $L=M_{\bar x}$ with $P\oplus_E G$, the quotient of $P\times G$ by the congruence generated by $(p+e,u)\sim(p,f(e)+u)$ for $e\in E$. Write every monoid additively, including the abstract abelian group $G$, and let $f:E\to G$ be induced by $\beta$. Since $P$ is fs it is integral, $E$ is a submonoid and $G$ is an abelian group, so [lem-sfb-integral-monoid-unit-pushout] applies and $L$ is integral: its canonical map to $L^{\rm gp}$ is injective. This application permits a noninjective $f$ and arbitrary torsion in $G$ and $P^{\rm gp}$. Let $\iota:E^{\rm gp}\to P^{\rm gp}$ be induced by the inclusion, $f^{\rm gp}:E^{\rm gp}\to G$ the extension of $f$, and put\n$$K=(P^{\rm gp}\oplus G)/\{(\iota(z),-f^{\rm gp}(z)):z\in E^{\rm gp}\}.$$

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69, etale fs charts; VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, localization convention. Agent application of the cited mixed-pushout embedding.

proof.text:
The displayed $K$ is $L^{m gp}$, with canonical map $[p,u]\mapsto[(p,u)]$: a monoid map $L	o B$ to an abelian group is exactly a pair of monoid maps from $P$ and $G$ whose composites with $E\subseteq P$ and $f$ agree on $E$; extend the first uniquely to $P^{m gp}$ and factor through the displayed subgroup, on which the two maps agree because they agree on $E$ and every element of $E^{m gp}$ is a difference $e_1-e_2$. This gives the group-completion universal property, so by step 1 the map $L	o K$ is injective. To check saturation, let $k=[(v,u)]\in K$ and suppose $nk=[(p,w)]$ for $n>0$, $p\in P$, $w\in G$. Equality in the quotient gives $e_1,e_2\in E$ with $nv-p=e_1-e_2$ in $P^{m gp}$. Consequently
$$n(v+e_2)=p+e_1+(n-1)e_2\in P.$$
Saturation of $P$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $v+e_2\in P$. Adding the defining subgroup element $(e_2,-f(e_2))$ shows
$$k=[(v+e_2,u-f(e_2))]\in L.$$
Together with the integrality of step 1, this proves that every geometric log stalk is integral and saturated. The argument uses only addition and the definition of saturation; it never divides by $n$ or assumes that multiplication by $n$ is injective.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101, root saturation; agent elementary calculation in the mixed-pushout quotient of step 1.

proof.text: We first make precise equality detection for the sheaf $M$. For any etale $V\to X$, suppose $a,b\in M(V)$ have equal germs at every geometric point of $V$. The finite-equalities clause of [lem-trf-finite-monoid-stalk-data-spreading] gives, at each such point, a pointed etale refinement $W\to V$ on which $a=b$; its restriction-stalk clause identifies the germs with the stalks on $X$ used above. Choosing one geometric point over each point of $V$, these refinements form a jointly surjective etale covering. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] gives $a=b$ on $V$. Now map $M(V)$ to the product of $M_{\bar v}^{\rm gp}$ for those geometric points. Step 1 embeds each stalk in its group completion, and equality detection makes this monoid map injective. Its extension through $M(V)^{\rm gp}$ implies that the canonical map $M(V)\to M(V)^{\rm gp}$ is injective. Also $M(V)$ is cancellative: an equality $a+c=b+c$ can be cancelled in that group and then pulled back through the injection. This holds for every $V$, including the fibre products used in gluing below.

source.place: Tags 03PQ (lemma-cofinal-etale) and 040R (definition-stalk and the following elementwise description); sheaf equalizer: sites.tex, Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets). Agent deduction of separation and integrality.

proof.text: Let $U\to X$ be etale, $H=M(U)$, $g\in H^{\rm gp}$, and $ng=j(c)$ for $c\in H$ and $n>0$. Write $g=j(a)-j(b)$ with $a,b\in H$: in the generators-and-relations group completion [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], every finite word is the difference of its positive and negative sums. At a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$, apply the group homomorphism induced by the germ map. The element $g_{\bar u}=a_{\bar u}-b_{\bar u}$ has $ng_{\bar u}=c_{\bar u}$, so step 2 gives $t_{\bar u}\in M_{\bar u}$ representing $g_{\bar u}$. Integrality of the stalk implies the equality $t_{\bar u}+b_{\bar u}=a_{\bar u}$ in the monoid. By the representatives and finite-equalities clauses of [lem-trf-finite-monoid-stalk-data-spreading], this element and equality lift to a pointed etale refinement $V_{\bar u}\to U$ and a section $t_{\bar u,V}\in M(V_{\bar u})$ satisfying $t_{\bar u,V}+b|_{V_{\bar u}}=a|_{V_{\bar u}}$. Choosing these refinements over every point of $U$ gives an etale cover.

source.place: Tag 040R (definition-stalk and subsequent representatives/eventual-equality description), Tag 03PQ (lemma-cofinal-etale); ILO VIII 3.1.17, p.101, supplies the root-saturation definition.

proof.text: On $V_i\times_U V_j$, both lifted sections satisfy $t_i+b=a=t_j+b$. Cancellation for sections, established for every etale object in step 3, gives $t_i=t_j$ on that fibre product. The sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] therefore glues them to a section $t\in M(U)$. The equality $t+b=a$ holds globally by the uniqueness part of the same equalizer, since it holds on the cover. In $H^{\rm gp}$ it gives $j(t)=j(a)-j(b)=g$. Hence $g\in j(H)$, which is the required saturation.

source.place: Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets, equalizer and the following gluing formulation; agent application using cancellation from step 3.

proof.text: The argument imposed no quasi-compactness on $U$ and used no finite generation of its sections. For $U=\varnothing$, the empty covering and the sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] make $M(U)$ a singleton, whose group completion is the zero group; injectivity and saturation hold directly. For $U=X$ the same argument applies to the identity etale object. No step assumed torsion freeness: the gluing uniqueness used $t+b=a$ and cancellation, rather than uniqueness of an $n$-th root.

source.place: Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets, including the empty covering; agent edge-case check.
